turns.answer:
I couldn't call the Concierge: a hook blocks the Agent tool in this session. So I found the files myself and this is a draft only. Nothing in the palace has changed.

The pitch lives in `Projects/Loudon Live/Loudon Live — launch kit.md`: the tagline, the About text, the short bio, the trailer and the title patterns. It was written in May, before the page was narrowed on 2026-10-14 to your teaching and coaching face. So it says nothing about LDN RTM or coaching. `Projects/Loudon Live.md:59` says the page wins when they disagree, so I followed the page.

**One tension, said once.** The palace's own measure is "How do you feel?" not "How many views?" (Hilaritas Generator § The Metrics). It's your channel, so I did what you asked. Two things I didn't bend: nothing goes in that isn't true, and titles still make no promises about results (`Loudon Live.md:66`). They mostly pull the same way anyway. The current copy loses clicks by being vague, and concrete copy is both more clickable and more honest.

## Tagline

> **How sound works, built live.**

Backup: *Synths, effects and the ears that judge them — built on stream.*

## About (YouTube)

Search results and previews show only the first line or so, so the hook goes first and your name comes second.

> Synths, effects and music tools, built live — plus the sound theory and music technique that make them worth building.
>
> I'm Loudon. I've spent a long time teaching music, and here I teach the way I learned: by making things. Each stream pushes one project forward — a synth from scratch, an effect from first principles, a product manual read cover to cover and tested — and I talk through every decision, including the ones that don't work yet.
>
> Come for: sound design from first principles · DSP you can hear · instrument building · listening and music technique · gear manuals, section by section (LDN RTM).
>
> New streams [DAY] at [TIME]. Every stream stays up, with chapters. Subscribe to catch them live.
> One-on-one coaching: [link]

**Short bio:** *Synths, effects and music tools, built live. Learn how sound works while it's working.*

## Titles

This is the biggest lever. The current patterns (`Sound lab · [topic]`) put the series label where the hook should be. Flip them: the question or the thing comes first, the series tag last.

- `What makes a sound feel warm? · Sound lab`
- `Shepard tones: the sound that rises forever · Sound lab`
- `A wavetable synth shaped like a donut · Live build`
- `Building a delay from scratch · Live build`
- `[Product] manual, every page tested · RTM #[N]`

The RTM titles will probably bring the most views. People search for a product by name, and the format answers that search. Putting the tool in the title doesn't break "not a tools brand" (`Loudon Live.md:83`). The format is about a tool; the channel isn't.

## Trailer (~50 sec)

Viewers decide in the first five seconds, so open on a sound, not a hello. The work-in-progress note shrinks to one line, which is also what the page says to do (`Loudon Live.md:85`).

> *[Cold open, ~3 sec: a Shepard tone climbing.]*
>
> That sound keeps climbing, and it never gets any higher. Stick around and I'll show you how.
>
> I'm Loudon. On Loudon Live I build synths, effects and music tools, live, and talk through every decision: the physics of the sound, the technique, and what your ears are actually doing. I've spent a long time teaching music; this is how I teach now.
>
> One project per stream. Some go deep on how sound works. Some are builds. Some are me hitting a wall and getting past it, and those are often the best ones.
>
> The channel's new and still finding its shape. The work is real.
>
> Subscribe, and I'll see you on stream.

## What I didn't check

- The donut line comes from the torus-geometry note on the page (`Loudon Live.md:102`). I didn't open the synth's own page, so check that it fits.
- "A long time teaching music" is your own wording from the kit. I didn't check it any further.
- I left thumbnails out. Anything visual means reading the Loudon Live Design System first, and I haven't.

Putting this into the launch kit is a change to the house, and without the Concierge only an elder can make it. Say "grow up" and I'll write it, or take it to a session where the Concierge can be called.

The kit's last line still applies: read it out loud first. How does it sound in your voice?
